\chapter{Chapter06 — Spectral Degree}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from FABL.Chapter06.F₂Polynomials.SpectralDegree
\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter06.F₂Polynomials.SpectralDegree}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Support of an indexed binary vector]
\lean{FABL.indexedF₂Support}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.𝔽₂}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p149-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p149-b004
}
For a finite index set $\iota$ and a function $x\colon\iota\to\mathbb{F}_2$, its support
is the set of indices $i$ for which $x(i)\ne 0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Finset indicator on a finite index type]
\lean{FABL.indexedF₂CubeOfFinset}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.𝔽₂}
Let $\iota$ be a finite type and let $S$ be a finite subset of $\iota$. Its indicator is
the function from $\iota$ to $\mathbb{F}_2$ that equals $1$ on $S$ and $0$ outside $S$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Binary cube and subset correspondence]
\lean{FABL.indexedF₂CubeEquivFinset}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.indexedF₂CubeOfFinset, FABL.indexedF₂Support, FABL.𝔽₂}
For a finite index set $\iota$, the map from functions $x:\iota\to\mathbb{F}_2$ to
subsets of $\iota$ sends each function to its support, the set of indices where it is
nonzero. This map is an equivalence, with inverse given by the indicator function of a
subset.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Sign cube and subset correspondence]
\lean{FABL.indexedSignCubeEquivFinset}
\label{FABL.indexedSignCubeEquivFinset}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IndexedSignCube, FABL.binarySignEquiv, FABL.indexedF₂CubeEquivFinset}
For a finite index set $\iota$, the map from sign assignments $x:\iota\to\{+1,-1\}$ to
subsets of $\iota$ sends each assignment to the indices where its sign corresponds to
the nonzero element of $\mathbb{F}_2$. This map is an equivalence, with inverse given by
the corresponding sign assignment of each subset.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Free frequency and powerset correspondence]
\lean{FABL.freeFrequencyPowersetEquiv}
\label{FABL.freeFrequencyPowersetEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.freeFrequencyPart, FABL.liftFreeFrequency, FABL.mem_freeFrequencyPart}
Let $J$ be a subset of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. The free frequencies supported on $J$ are in
bijection with the subsets of $J$: a free frequency is sent to its set of indices, and a
subset is sent to the corresponding free frequency.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Constant positive sign assignment]
\lean{FABL.zeroFixedSign}
\label{FABL.zeroFixedSign}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedSignCube}
Let $J$ be a subset of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. On the indices outside $J$, define the sign
assignment that takes the value $+1$ at every index.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Binary point from free signs]
\lean{FABL.binaryPointOfFreeSign_eq_f₂CubeOfFinset}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedIndex, FABL.FreeSignCube, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv, FABL.binarySignEquiv, FABL.combineSignCube, FABL.combineSignCube_apply_fixed, FABL.combineSignCube_apply_free, FABL.f₂CubeOfFinset, FABL.f₂CubeOfFinset_apply, FABL.indexedF₂Support, FABL.indexedSignCubeEquivFinset, FABL.liftFreeFrequency, FABL.zeroFixedSign}
\difficulty{5}
For every $n$, every set $J$ of coordinates in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and every assignment
$y$ of signs to the coordinates in $J$, combine $y$ with the constant $+1$ assignment on
the remaining coordinates and convert the resulting sign vector to a binary vector. This
binary vector is the indicator vector, over $\mathbb F_2$, of the set of coordinates in
$J$ where $y$ equals $-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Free-coordinate sum and ANF coefficient]
\lean{FABL.sum_freeSignCube_boolean_eq_anfCoeff}
\label{FABL.sum_freeSignCube_boolean_eq_anfCoeff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FreeSignCube, FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.anfCoeff, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv, FABL.binaryPointOfFreeSign_eq_f₂CubeOfFinset, FABL.combineSignCube, FABL.freeFrequencyPowersetEquiv, FABL.f₂CubeOfFinset, FABL.indexedSignCubeEquivFinset, FABL.liftFreeFrequency, FABL.zeroFixedSign}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f$ be a function from the binary cube of dimension $n$ to $\mathbb F_2$, and let
$S$ be a subset of the coordinate set. Sum, in $\mathbb F_2$, the values of $f$ over
all binary inputs whose coordinates outside $S$ are zero and whose coordinates in $S$
vary freely. This sum equals the algebraic normal form coefficient of $f$ indexed by
$S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Indexed sign monomial]
\lean{FABL.indexedMonomialInt}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p022-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p148-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p149-b001
}
\label{FABL.indexedMonomialInt}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IndexedSignCube}
For a finite subset $S$ of an index type $\iota$, a function $x\colon\iota\to\{\pm1\}$,
and signs viewed as integers, the indexed monomial is $\prod_{i\in S}x(i)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Integer and real indexed monomials]
\lean{FABL.indexedMonomialInt_cast}
\label{FABL.indexedMonomialInt_cast}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IndexedSignCube, FABL.indexedMonomial, FABL.indexedMonomialInt, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{1}
For any index type, any finite set $S$ of indices, and any assignment of signs to those
indices, the integer product of the signs over $S$, interpreted as a real number, equals
the real monomial over $S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Indexed sign product modulo two]
\lean{FABL.indexedMonomialInt_cast_f₂_eq_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IndexedSignCube, FABL.indexedMonomialInt, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{3}
For any index type, any finite set $S$ of indices, and any assignment of signs to those
indices, the integer product of the signs over $S$, reduced modulo $2$, equals $1$ in
the field with two elements.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p148-b003}
Let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2$ be a Boolean function, let $S\subseteq[n]$ have
nonzero algebraic normal form coefficient, and let $A\subseteq S$. Restrict the
corresponding real-valued sign-cube function by fixing every coordinate outside $S$ to
$+1$, and take its Fourier coefficient on the free-coordinate set $A$. This coefficient
is an odd integer divided by $2^{|S|}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A maximal-degree nonzero ANF coefficient]
\lean{FABL.exists_top_anfCoeff}
\label{FABL.exists_top_anfCoeff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.algebraicDegree, FABL.anfCoeff, FABL.anfEval, FABL.anfEval_anfCoeff, FABL.anfSupport, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree, FABL.mem_anfSupport}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f$ be a nonzero Boolean function on $\mathbb F_2^n$. There is a set
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ whose algebraic normal form coefficient is nonzero and whose
cardinality equals the algebraic degree of $f$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.restrictionFourierCoeff_granular}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p072-b003,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p076-b001}
Let $n$ and $k$ be nonnegative integers, and let $f$ be a function from the
$n$-dimensional cube over the field with two elements to that field. Regard $f$ as a
real-valued function on this cube by mapping its value $1$ to $1$ and its value $0$ to
$0$, and transfer this function to the sign cube $\{-1,1\}^n$ using the coordinatewise
correspondence between binary values and signs. If every Fourier coefficient of the
resulting function is an integer multiple of $2^{-k}$, then the algebraic degree of $f$
is at most $k$.
\end{theorem}
